verses.english: This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

verses.pali: “Saṅghāṭikaṇṇe cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gahetvā piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandho assa pāde pādaṁ nikkhipanto,
verses.english: “Mendicants, suppose a mendicant were to hold the corner of my cloak and follow behind me step by step.

verses.pali: so ca hoti abhijjhālu kāmesu tibbasārāgo byāpannacitto paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo muṭṭhassati asampajāno asamāhito vibbhantacitto pākatindriyo;
verses.english: Yet they covet sensual pleasures; they’re infatuated, full of ill will and malicious intent. They are unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

verses.pali: atha kho so ārakāva mayhaṁ, ahañca tassa.
verses.english: Then they are far from me, and I from them.

verses.pali: Dhammañhi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na passati.
verses.english: Because that mendicant does not see the teaching.
Not seeing the teaching, they do not see me.

verses.pali: Yojanasate cepi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vihareyya.
verses.english: Suppose a mendicant were to live a hundred leagues away.

verses.pali: So ca hoti anabhijjhālu kāmesu na tibbasārāgo abyāpannacitto apaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo upaṭṭhitassati sampajāno samāhito ekaggacitto saṁvutindriyo;
verses.english: Yet they do not covet sensual pleasures; they’re not infatuated, or full of ill will and malicious intent. They have established mindfulness, situational awareness and immersion, with unified mind and restrained faculties.

verses.pali: atha kho so santikeva mayhaṁ, ahañca tassa.
verses.english: Then they are close to me, and I to them.
Because that mendicant sees the teaching.
Seeing the teaching, they see me.”
yet see how distant they are—
An astute person who has understood
as a lake free of wind.

verses.pali: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
verses.english: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
